facts: INSPIRE Index Polygons show the indicative extent and position of registered freehold properties in England and Wales.
The current public INSPIRE files were published on 5 July 2026.
HM Land Registry states that new INSPIRE files are published on the first Sunday of every month.
INSPIRE polygon files are downloadable by local authority.
Viewing the downloaded polygons requires GIS software.
Downloading the dataset is subject to Open Government Licence conditions.
guards: Treat the July 2026 publication date as source-freshness evidence, not as proof that any candidate boundary is exact.
Require the local-authority source file used for a candidate to be recorded in provenance.
Reject candidate promotion when the source file month cannot be identified.
Do not infer title ownership attributes that are not present in the INSPIRE candidate geometry.
Do not treat GIS display success as boundary-accuracy proof.
Preserve OGL attribution/provenance with any derived candidate record.

facts: INSPIRE polygons are explicitly described as indicative extent and position data.
A registered estate boundary is a general boundary unless shown as determined under section 60 of the Land Registration Act 2002.
A determined boundary is the mechanism that makes the exact line apparent from the register.
HM Land Registry does not resolve the exact line simply by displaying an index polygon.
Determined-boundary evidence is retained through the filed determined-boundary plan.
Candidate-location geometry and exact-boundary evidence are therefore different evidence classes.
guards: Classify INSPIRE geometry as candidate-location evidence only.
Never label an INSPIRE polygon as an exact legal boundary.
Require a separate exact-boundary evidence class before parcel-edge elevation sampling is promoted.
Keep general-boundary/title-plan and determined-boundary evidence fields separate.
Fail closed when the evidence class for a proposed boundary edge is unknown.
Do not publish a height-difference result merely because an INSPIRE polygon intersects a terrain raster.

facts: Ordnance Survey mapping shows topographic features and is not intended to represent property boundaries.
Map position can vary from the real-world position because of specified accuracy tolerances.
Distances scaled from OS mapping may not exactly equal distances measured on the ground.
A line on a 1:1250 OS map roughly represents 0.3 metres on the ground.
A line on a 1:2500 OS map roughly represents 0.6 metres on the ground.
Map-scale uncertainty is materially larger than millimetre-level determined-boundary measurement tolerances.
guards: Reject sub-decimetre boundary claims derived only from ordinary OS map line placement.
Record source map scale whenever a mapped feature is used as contextual boundary evidence.
Treat 1:1250 and 1:2500 line-width effects as uncertainty, not measurement precision.
Do not use displayed line-centre coordinates as a substitute for determined-boundary survey evidence.
Require independent exact-boundary evidence before using mapped topographic features as sampling edges.
Prevent map-display resolution from being misreported as legal-boundary accuracy.

facts: A determined-boundary plan must clearly show the extent of boundary to be determined.
The plan must identify start, end and turning points, preferably with lettered points.
The plan must contain sufficient surrounding detail to relate the boundary to OS mapping.
The plan must show orientation, for example a north point.
The preferred plan scale is no smaller than 1:200.
The plan must not include disclaimers that cast doubt on accuracy, such as for identification purposes only.
guards: Require explicit start/end/turning-point geometry before accepting a determined-boundary line for sampling.
Reject a candidate exact-boundary line if its orientation/context cannot be related to surrounding mapped detail.
Record stated survey-plan scale with any exact-boundary geometry.
Do not promote plans carrying accuracy-disclaiming wording.
Reject a boundary line reconstructed only from a cropped image without control/context.
Require the exact boundary segment used for elevation sampling to be traceable to the filed plan evidence.

facts: Measurements on a determined-boundary plan must be accurate to plus or minus 10 millimetres.
Measurements must be taken horizontally rather than along a slope.
Measurements must be taken from at least two defined points on surrounding permanent physical features.
HM Land Registry prefers control from both sides of the boundary where possible.
Permanent features are expected reasonably to remain in position for at least 10 years.
Features subject to natural growth or decay are not acceptable measurement references.
guards: Reject slope-distance values where horizontal distance is required.
Require at least two defined stable control points before accepting measurement-based exact-boundary reconstruction.
Reject trees, hedges and other naturally changing features as exact survey controls.
Store the measurement-accuracy certificate/evidence when present.
Do not treat terrain raster resolution as a replacement for survey control accuracy.
Keep boundary-location uncertainty separate from vertical terrain uncertainty in the final error budget.

facts: Only National Grid coordinates are accepted for coordinate-based determined-boundary plans.
National Grid coordinates used this way must have absolute accuracy of plus or minus 300 millimetres.
They must have relative accuracy of plus or minus 10 millimetres.
Coordinates are recorded as metric eastings and northings.
A qualified professional must certify the stated coordinate accuracy.
Greater certified absolute accuracy than plus or minus 300 millimetres is acceptable.
guards: Reject coordinate-based exact-boundary evidence with an unknown CRS.
Require British National Grid/National Grid coordinate provenance before using coordinate controls.
Do not confuse absolute coordinate accuracy with relative inter-point accuracy.
Require eastings/northings ordering to be explicit before geometry construction.
Preserve the professional accuracy certificate reference in provenance.
Do not claim better coordinate accuracy than the certificate supports.

facts: Environment Agency Composite DTM 1m covers about 99 percent of England at 1 metre spatial resolution.
The DTM removes surface objects to model the terrain surface.
The 2022 composite combines Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where repeat surveys exist, the newest best-resolution data is used.
The dataset is supplied as GeoTIFF rasters in 5 kilometre tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
Elevations are in metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn using the OSTN15 transformation method.
guards: Require tile identity and survey-provenance metadata for every promoted elevation sample.
Reject a height sample when the vertical datum is unknown.
Reject a height sample when horizontal grid alignment/CRS is unknown.
Do not mix DSM surface heights with DTM ground heights.
Record whether a sample came from composite or time-stamped source data.
Do not promote a numeric height-difference row until both boundary and elevation provenance are complete.

facts: The 2022 composite contains source surveys undertaken from 6 June 2000 through 2 April 2022.
Metadata indexes identify which survey contributed at a given location.
Resampled source data used bilinear interpolation before merging.
All individual LIDAR surveys entering the composite had vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15 centimetres RMSE.
The composite may therefore combine source surveys from materially different dates.
One-metre raster spacing does not mean one-centimetre or millimetre vertical accuracy.
guards: Require source-survey date metadata for candidate acceptance where temporal change could matter.
Carry plus or minus 15 centimetre RMSE source accuracy into the measurement-quality assessment.
Flag resampled cells separately from native-resolution source cells when provenance exposes that distinction.
Do not treat 1 metre pixel size as vertical error.
Do not compare elevations from mismatched survey epochs without recording the temporal mismatch.
Fail closed when the metadata index cannot identify the contributing survey for a proposed official sample.

facts: OS Terrain 5 grid uses regular 5 metre post spacing.
Grid height values are calculated as a mean of heights across the whole 5 metre pixel.
ASCII z values are positioned at pixel centres.
A 5 km tile contains 1000 rows of 1000 pixels.
Height values are written to the nearest 0.01 metre in ASCII grid files.
The GML companion supplies metadata and spatial reference information while height data is held in the external ASCII block.
guards: Do not interpret 0.01 metre numeric storage precision as 0.01 metre measurement accuracy.
Record whether a cross-check uses pixel-centre/mean-cell semantics.
Do not compare a point LIDAR sample and a 5 metre cell mean as though they were identical measurement operators.
Require the correct ASC/GML/metadata files to remain associated with a tile provenance record.
Reject a Terrain 5 cross-check when tile placement/header coordinates cannot be verified.
Use Terrain 5 as a coarser cross-check unless the product accuracy and sampling semantics support a stronger claim.

facts: OS Terrain 5 is supplied in 5 km by 5 km tiles.
Tiles are identified by the National Grid reference of their south-west corner.
OS Terrain 5 GML expresses its coordinate reference system as EPSG 27700.
The product is updated by whole-tile refresh rather than feature-level change-only updates.
Feature identifiers may be regenerated when a tile is updated.
OS Terrain 5 is updated quarterly.
guards: Record Terrain 5 tile version/release provenance with every cross-check.
Do not use feature identifiers alone as stable cross-release provenance.
Require EPSG:27700 alignment or a documented transformation before cross-source comparison.
Reject stale cached tile assumptions when a newer quarterly tile is used.
Use the south-west National Grid tile reference to validate tile placement.
Prevent cross-release comparisons from silently mixing different Terrain 5 tile generations.

facts: HMLR INSPIRE polygons provide candidate spatial geometry for registered freehold properties.
EA DTM tiles are aligned to the OS National Grid.
OS Terrain 5 geometries use EPSG:27700 British National Grid.
All three sources can therefore be handled in a British National Grid workflow when source CRS is preserved.
INSPIRE boundary semantics remain indicative even when coordinate systems align.
Coordinate-system compatibility does not upgrade legal-boundary evidence quality.
guards: Require candidate geometry and terrain raster to be in the same verified horizontal CRS before overlay.
Do not let successful spatial intersection promote an indicative polygon to exact-boundary status.
Store source CRS per input rather than assuming it from file extension.
Reject silent reprojection without recording transformation/provenance.
Separate horizontal alignment PASS from legal-boundary evidence PASS.
Separate horizontal alignment PASS from vertical-datum PASS.

facts: EA source surveys contributing to the DTM have plus or minus 15 centimetre RMSE vertical accuracy.
OS Terrain 5 grid values represent mean heights over 5 metre pixels.
Determined-boundary measurements can require plus or minus 10 millimetre measurement accuracy.
Boundary-position error and elevation error are different error components.
Raster resolution, storage precision and survey accuracy are different concepts.
A defensible parcel height-difference result must preserve these distinctions.
guards: Do not report more decimal precision than the combined evidence justifies.
Keep legal-boundary location uncertainty and terrain vertical uncertainty as separate fields.
Require sample operator metadata such as point, pixel mean or zonal statistic.
Reject a result whose apparent height difference is not meaningfully larger than its uncertainty budget.
Do not derive confidence from numeric formatting alone.
Promote an official measured row only after boundary, CRS, vertical datum, tile/survey provenance and integrity readback all pass.
